title: Capstone 1: End‑to‑End Image Classifier 🖼️
description: Go from zero to a fully trained and converted TFLite model, ready for a mobile app.

slides.title: The Mission 🎯
slides.content:
# Build a Complete Image Classifier

You have a folder of images of **five animal species** (cat, dog, bird, fish, horse). You want an app that can recognise them from the camera.

We'll:
1. Load and preprocess the images with `tf.data`.
2. Build and fine‑tune a MobileNetV2 model.
3. Apply Quantization‑Aware Training.
4. Convert to TFLite with metadata.
5. Write a simple Task Library caller (conceptual).

All steps in one notebook – this is the capstone of everything you've learned.

slides.title: Step 1: Load and Augment Data
slides.content: Use `image_dataset_from_directory` to create training and validation sets.
slides.codeSnippet:
import tensorflow as tf

IMG_SIZE = (224, 224)
BATCH = 32

train_ds = tf.keras.utils.image_dataset_from_directory(
    'animals/train',
    validation_split=0.2,
    subset='training',
    seed=42,
    image_size=IMG_SIZE,
    batch_size=BATCH
)
val_ds = tf.keras.utils.image_dataset_from_directory(
    'animals/train',
    validation_split=0.2,
    subset='validation',
    seed=42,
    image_size=IMG_SIZE,
    batch_size=BATCH
)

# Prefetch for performance
train_ds = train_ds.prefetch(tf.data.AUTOTUNE)
val_ds = val_ds.prefetch(tf.data.AUTOTUNE)

slides.title: Step 2: Build the Model (Transfer Learning)
slides.content:
# MobileNetV2 Base + Custom Head

Freeze the base, add GlobalAveragePooling, Dropout, Dense with softmax.

We'll also add data augmentation layers at the start to keep the model self‑contained.

slides.title: Model Architecture
slides.codeSnippet:
from tensorflow.keras import layers, models

data_augmentation = tf.keras.Sequential([
    layers.RandomFlip('horizontal'),
    layers.RandomRotation(0.1),
    layers.RandomZoom(0.1)
])

base_model = tf.keras.applications.MobileNetV2(
    weights='imagenet', include_top=False, input_shape=(224,224,3)
)
base_model.trainable = False

inputs = tf.keras.Input(shape=(224,224,3))
x = data_augmentation(inputs)
# Preprocess for MobileNetV2
x = tf.keras.applications.mobilenet_v2.preprocess_input(x)
x = base_model(x, training=False)
x = layers.GlobalAveragePooling2D()(x)
x = layers.Dropout(0.2)(x)
outputs = layers.Dense(5, activation='softmax')(x)
model = tf.keras.Model(inputs, outputs)

slides.title: Step 3: Train (Feature Extraction Phase)
slides.content:
# Compile and Fit

```python
model.compile(optimizer='adam', loss='sparse_categorical_crossentropy', metrics=['accuracy'])
history = model.fit(train_ds, validation_data=val_ds, epochs=10)
```

After this, the head is trained. Now we can fine‑tune.

slides.title: Step 4: Fine‑tune and QAT
slides.content: Unfreeze some base layers, then apply Quantization‑Aware Training.
slides.codeSnippet:
# Fine‑tune
base_model.trainable = True
for layer in base_model.layers[:-20]:
    layer.trainable = False
model.compile(optimizer=tf.keras.optimizers.Adam(1e-5), loss='sparse_categorical_crossentropy', metrics=['accuracy'])
model.fit(train_ds, validation_data=val_ds, epochs=5)

# QAT
import tensorflow_model_optimization as tfmot
qat_model = tfmot.quantization.keras.quantize_model(model)
qat_model.compile(optimizer='adam', loss='sparse_categorical_crossentropy', metrics=['accuracy'])
qat_model.fit(train_ds, validation_data=val_ds, epochs=3)

slides.title: Step 5: Convert to TFLite with Metadata
slides.content:
# Add Metadata for Task Library

- Convert the QAT model.
- Use the TFLite Metadata Writer to embed labels and normalization info.
- The resulting model is ready for `ImageClassifier.createFromFile` on Android.

slides.title: Conversion & Metadata
slides.codeSnippet:
converter = tf.lite.TFLiteConverter.from_keras_model(qat_model)
converter.optimizations = [tf.lite.Optimize.DEFAULT]
tflite_model = converter.convert()

# Save model
with open('animal_classifier.tflite', 'wb') as f:
    f.write(tflite_model)

# (Optional: use flatbuffers to add label file and metadata – see documentation)

slides.title: You Did It! 🎉
slides.content: This pipeline is exactly what professional ML engineers use. You've taken raw images to a production‑ready mobile model.
